confusions: The 'Keep code easy to review' recipe says to tag legacy objects and put the tag in CONV-040 except_tags. The workspace has no such tag, and the skill says to propose a missing tag rather than write it. The rule is therefore written without an exemption; the recipe's first step has to be done by the owner first, and the skill does not say how to phrase that to a customer.

The recipe puts CONV-040 in its own policy, but CONV-040 and the 'Endpoints and functions stay short' template share one check (stack.size_limit) with CONV-041. I did not know whether two policies with the same check would conflict; I kept only CONV-040.

The policy 'Keep code easy to review' recipe lists 'functions say what they do' as an extra rule, but the template catalogue does not have a template for it. Fine as a custom policy, but the key I chose (REVIEW-010) is my own invention.

xano policy parse output omitted 'severity = "medium"' from LOG-010 and PERF-001 when printing back, while it kept 'severity = "low"' on the others. It parsed without error; I could not tell whether medium is the default and dropped silently.

The skill says 'Build rules only from the catalogue', and the templates' examples are empty ({}). For PERF-001, 'max: 1000' came from the template summary, not an example; that was fine but had to be read from the summary text.

The skill says 'Never say a policy will stop merges' and that a blocking policy blocks a merge or push. The customer's words, 'stop juniors breaking prod', pull towards blocking. The skill says advisory for new policies and not to decide blocking myself; I followed that and explain in reply.md.
wished_for: A short 'customer words to policy' table for code review: 'breaking prod' should point to advisory-vs-blocking guidance, not only to the templates.
A note in the templates that CONV-040 counts statements, not lines, with a rough conversion from lines to statements.
A recipe step saying how to propose tags to a customer in plain words ('add a legacy tag to these objects') instead of only 'propose it separately'.
Clarity on whether two policies that share a check (CONV-040 and CONV-041) conflict or are checked separately.
Clarity on whether xano policy evaluate is needed to produce predicted object matches, since my run was forbidden and my predictions are unverified.
why_confidence: The five template policies and the description rule match the recipe and each parses clean (6 of 6 on the first try). But the ask is about stopping breakage and review load in general: the policies check error handling around api.request only, test existence rather than test quality, and statements rather than lines, and they are advisory so they do not stop anything on their own. I could not run xano policy evaluate (forbidden here), so the object matches in reply.md are predictions from reading the workspace, not evaluated findings.
